assumptions.text: 题目为六年级分数四则运算单选题（4 个选项），题目与答案由种子数据提供，管理员可增删改。

assumptions.text: 开始/结束动画以 CSS 过渡和文本场景实现，不依赖外部图片或视频素材。
assumptions.impact: 影响前端资源与打包体积；不阻塞核心流程。

assumptions.text: 无障碍要求：键盘可操作、语义化标签、可见焦点、颜色对比度不低于 4.5:1。

assumptions.text: 保留 Game/Question/User 三个服务边界，使用 REST + 进程内仓库运行；PostgreSQL 以可选适配器提供，Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/Kubernetes/Istio/Vault/Terraform 不纳入演示依赖。这是相对原文档微服务/云原生方案的重大偏离，必须在报告与 ASSUMPTIONS.md 中声明。

plan.summary: A web-based, interactive learning tool for sixth-grade students to practice fraction-solving skills. The implementation uses modular microservice-style boundaries inside a single Node.js process so that all requirements can be verified without external cloud services. The browser UI provides play, score, and help views; administration is protected by an environment-configured token; question data is persisted to a JSON file store to satisfy data durability and restart recovery.
plan.architecture_style: Microservice boundaries simulated as modular monolith with REST-style APIs

stack.persistence: JSON file repository with optional PostgreSQL adapter interface
stack.testing: Node.js built-in test runner with HTTP integration tests

deviations.decision: Simulate microservices as a modular monolith with service-route boundaries
deviations.reason: Enables local verification without Kubernetes, service discovery, or external cloud infrastructure while preserving Game, Question, User, and Admin component boundaries.
deviations.impact: Services are not network-isolated; the structure remains ready for later extraction into independent deployable services.

deviations.decision: Use file-backed JSON persistence as the default repository instead of PostgreSQL
deviations.reason: Meets ASR-1 data durability and restart recovery without requiring an external database service during verification.
deviations.impact: Lower operational realism and limited concurrent write durability compared to PostgreSQL; repository interfaces allow swapping to a database adapter later.

deviations.decision: Exclude Redis, RabbitMQ, Elasticsearch, Kubernetes, Istio, Vault, and Terraform from demonstration dependencies
deviations.reason: The source documentation did not provide business constraints or operational budgets for these components; they are treated as optional extensions.
deviations.impact: Reduces infrastructure fidelity but improves testability and runnable delivery.

deviations.decision: Formalize ASR-2 security as minimal admin token authentication, input validation, and security headers
deviations.reason: The source documentation referenced ASR-2 without a formal definition or acceptance metrics.
deviations.impact: Security coverage is implemented and tested, but it is a pragmatic interpretation rather than a documented enterprise security model.

deviations.decision: Resolve empty trace/test matrix and diagram syntax inconsistencies by deriving traceability from requirements and use cases
deviations.reason: The provided test matrix was empty and several PlantUML diagrams used non-native notation.
deviations.impact: Traceability is reconstructed from component and requirement statements; ambiguity remains for undocumented behaviors.

verification_steps: Run npm install to install dependencies.
Run npm test and confirm all unit, integration, security, performance, and restart recovery tests pass.
Run npm start and open http://localhost:3000 in a browser.
From the browser UI, start a game, answer ten questions, and verify the final score is displayed.
Open the help view and verify keyboard-only navigation is possible.
Use an admin token to create, update, and delete a question through the API, then restart the server and verify the change persists.
Attempt admin question update without a token and verify the request is rejected.
Stop and restart the server, then verify persisted questions and any persisted scores are recovered.
assumptions: A1: The game will be played by 1000 users concurrently.
A2: The game will be played for 1 hour per session.
ASM-01: Each game has exactly 10 fraction questions; correct answers add 10 points, wrong answers add 0 points, maximum score is 100, and there is no countdown timer.
ASM-02: Students do not register; a guest ID is generated at the start of each session, and scores are only shown for the current round. Administrators log in with an environment-configured token.
ASM-03: Questions are sixth-grade single-choice fraction arithmetic items with 4 answer choices, seeded by data and manageable by administrators.
ASM-04: Start/end animations use CSS transitions and text scenes only, with no external image or video assets.
ASM-05: Accessibility requirements include keyboard operability, semantic markup, visible focus, and color contrast of at least 4.5:1.

ASM-06: Game, Question, and User service boundaries are preserved with REST plus in-process repositories; PostgreSQL is an optional adapter, and Redis/RabbitMQ/Elasticsearch/Kubernetes/Istio/Vault/Terraform are not included as demo dependencies.
These assumptions, including ASM-01 through ASM-06, are implementation constraints and not reused as requirement IDs.
ASR-2 is interpreted as a security requirement covering admin authentication, input validation, and basic security headers because the source did not provide a formal definition.
The parsing warnings for ObjectDiagram and CollaborationDiagram1/2 are treated as source syntax issues; their element semantics are extracted and implemented according to the corresponding use cases.
The document conflict C-001 about 11 versus 13 PlantUML diagrams is accepted as source inconsistency without blocking implementation.
The empty trace and test matrices are reconstructed from requirement statements, component definitions, and derived use cases.
risks: JSON file persistence may not satisfy the performance and concurrency assumptions for 1000 simultaneous users in production; PostgreSQL or a scalable store should replace it outside local verification.
The modular monolith approach verifies component boundaries but not true network microservice behavior, so deployment risks remain unrecognized.
ASR-2 security is an inferred requirement and may be incomplete relative to formal security policies.
The source diagrams contain notation inconsistencies, so some interactions derived from them may be ambiguous or over-simplified.
The user interaction with the browser UI is manually verified; no full end-to-end browser automation is included.
